summary:
The sharpest signal right now is the across-the-board split between starting pitching and bullpen fatigue: every rating (R1-R4) carries a 3-game winning streak on SP picks and a 5-game losing streak on bullpen_fatigue, with that fatigue category sitting dead last in season hit rate (45-47%). That's not noise — it's consistent across all four engines, so any game tonight where SP and bullpen_fatigue disagree, side with SP and fade bullpen_fatigue outright. On the flip side, R2 is the engine to trust most in recent form: its 30-day strong-play window is 7-1 (88%, +6.0u) compared to R1 and R3 at 4-1 and R4 at 3-1. If R2 flags a strong play tonight that other ratings don't, give it extra weight. With no 7d/14d strong-play action logged yet (n=0 across the board), today's board hasn't generated a signal independent of that 30-day sample — so treat early plays as confirmation bets on categories already trending hot rather than new information.

On the category-agreement front, trends+sp remains the top combo at 58% (370-268, n=638), with trends+runs right behind at 57.3%. Any matchup tonight where trends, sp, and runs all align on the same side is as close to a go-zone as this model offers — especially if one of the model's proven teams is involved. MIL (69%, n=74, +18.0u strong), LAD (70%, n=56, +27.0u strong), BOS (70%, n=56, +19.0u strong), and TBR (70%, n=63, +21.0u strong) are the four teams the model has printed money on all year when liked; if any of them show up as the pick tonight with trends+sp agreement, that's the headline play. Conversely, fade confidence on NYY — the model is break-even at best there (49% overall, 39% on strong plays, -4.0u), so even a hot category combo pointing at the Yankees should get discounted relative to the four trusted teams above.
